headline: Copper Rebounds From 11-Month Low on Return of Risk Appetite
author: Bloomberg News

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 10:33 PM EST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Copper extended its rebound from an 11-month low alongside technology stocks in Asia, as risk appetite returned across markets after weeks of volatility fueled by concerns over the artificial intelligence trade.

The red metal rose as much as 4.4% to trade above $12,300 a ton on the London Metal Exchange, putting the market on track for the first weekly increase since early October. The technology sector in Asia was among the biggest gainers on Friday, while US equity-index futures also climbed.

"It's concentrated short-covering triggered by the rebound in US equities," said Harry Jiang, a trader at China-Base Ningbo Group Co. "With Chinese inventories still tight, a bounce like this makes perfect sense."

The prospect of US tariffs had prompted traders to ship huge volumes of copper to the US earlier this year, tightening markets elsewhere, but a short squeeze in China has recently created a lucrative trading opportunity. Logistics companies fielded a deluge of inquiries from traders seeking to ship the metal from the US to the Asian nation, with several shipments booked.

The Yangshan premium for imported cargoes hit a record $500 a ton last week, but has since dipped to $320, according to Shanghai Metals Market. That's still well above historical levels. The spread between China's physical spot price and benchmark futures has also dropped over the past week, but still remains at a substantial premium. Inventories monitored by the exchange edged higher.

Copper in London has pulled back rapidly after hitting a record near $15,000 a ton in September, with concerns over the sustainability of spending on AI data centers weighing on sentiment. Looming US interest-rate hikes added to the pressure. The red metal was 3.7% higher at $12,314.50 a ton on the LME as of 11:32 a.m. in Shanghai. Tin, zinc and aluminum also rallied on Friday.
